utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. As was announced yesterday, Judge Fluegge is, for urgent personal reason, unable to continue to sit in this case for a short period. We expect that it will last only one day. Judge Moloto and I have considered whether it would be in the interests of justice to continue to hear the case, and we are satisfied that it is. That's the reason why we are sitting 15 bis today. There are a few preliminary matters which we'd like to deal with before the witness enters the courtroom. For the first one, I'd like to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The next item I'd like to briefly deal with is associated exhibit with Witness Savo Bojanovic. The Chamber notes that on the 8th of September, the Defence filed a motion to file 18 exhibits associated with the Rule 92 ter statement of Witness Savo Bojanovic. The Chamber invites the Defence to consider reducing the number of associated exhibits by, for example, tendering some of these documents with the witness during examination-in-chief. The next matter I would like to briefly deal with are associated exhibits related to the statement of -- to the testimony -- the evidence given by Witness Kralj. I do understand that we have six exhibits now left, associated exhibits, that are tendered. Is the Prosecution ready to respond to ...

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And good morning, Your Honours. Your Honours, I spoke with Mr. McCloskey, he does not object to the admission of these six associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The six remaining associated exhibits. I will read the numbers one by one and invite Madam Registrar to assign a number. The first one, 65 ter 1D02206 receives number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D737, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. 1D02207 receives number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D738 Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. 1D02304.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number D739, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D739 is admitted. 1D02305.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number D740, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D740 is admitted. 14687.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D741, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. 24893.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D742, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Thank you, Madam Registrar. I think we've dealt with all of those. Then I do understand, Mr. Lukic, that there was one matter related to Witness Sarenac --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which you would like to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't have time yesterday to work on this issue at all. As you know, I was fully engaged in translation and preparing of cross -- documents for cross-examination of Witness Vlaski. So we would kindly ask you to extend our deadline for Sarenac until weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the deadline was exactly about what --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Today, the deadline was today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I know, but deadline to do what --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To reply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that cause any problem for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the deadline is extended until after the weekend, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And thanks --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Shall we say --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- to my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Shall we say Monday, midday?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The deadline has been -- has been moved to Monday, the -- Monday is the 10th, midday. Then I do understand that the -- Mr. Vlaski's information report, that a translation was produced yesterday. The Chamber gave permission to hand out a copy of the B/C/S version through VWS to the witness so that at least an opening has been made to seek his attestation to that portion of his statement, to see whether it will be evidence before this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's understood, Your Honour. And the Prosecution would not have any objection to the Defence re-opening its examination for the purpose of laying that foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, would you prefer to deal with that matter before the Prosecution continues its cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm in your hands, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm afraid that I have not switched off my cell phone. I'll do it immediately. The witness can be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Just very briefly going back to the Kralj exhibits. We have -- I've been advised that with respect to one of the exhibits used with the witness, P6864, which was a cover letter and a series of convoy approvals, there were apparently a few pages in that exhibit that were not translated. We have submitted them and will advise both the Defence and the Chamber as soon as those are completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vlaski.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Vlaski, we were informed that you have been provided with a copy of the information report which contains, apart from a few other matters, primarily and mainly further explanations to your statement. Is that true? Have you received that in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did have -- receive the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to read it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Mr. Lukic will have an opportunity to put a few further questions to you in relation to this information report. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Vlaski.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we talked about working on the information report, on Saturday and Sunday, and this morning you say that you had the opportunity to read it in B/C/S; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did you find anything in the report that you did not tell me on Friday and Saturday?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that I said is reflected in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to put the same questions to you today as I put to you on Friday and Saturday, would you give the same answers?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would give the same answers with perhaps more detailed explanations for some questions because I have some additional evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is what you told me when we analysed your statement truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's all accurate and truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if there is nothing else, we would tender this information report into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, for some of the other reasons I already said, we ask that D736 marked for identification remain marked for identification. We do acknowledge that counsel has laid a foundation pursuant to Rule 92 ter at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is, then, D736 is now marked for identification. Has a -- has the B/C/S version been uploaded into e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Give us one second. I don't know if it's -- if it's in e-court. As you know, yesterday we had some problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. But then there's one remaining matter. If the witness would please be so kind to give the copy he received this morning to the usher so that the Prosecution and the Chamber also have an opportunity to verify whether what the witness attested to is the same as what we'll then later find in e-court because otherwise there is a missing link. Could the witness -- yes, Mr. Usher, could you please receive the copy from the -- and could it be put in the hands of the Registrar for the time -- for the time being. So the parties ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar keeps a copy which we just received from the witness so that the parties are in a position to verify whether the witness attested to the same as what then later appears in e-court. Having dealt with this matter, Mr. Weber, are you ready to continue your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vlaski.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yesterday at transcript page 27739, the Defence asked you a question about the documentation available to the State Security Service in Sarajevo. The question was: "Did it remain in Sarajevo or did you take it?" In a following answer on that same page, you did acknowledge that some of the documents were taken after military operations ensued. My question: Did you take any documents, recordings, or other material that belonged to the State Security Service in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents that were at the Zlatiste facility included documents from the previous period, and from what I know, a whole truck of documents was taken out of that facility. Yes, yes, I didn't see those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, that wasn't my question. I'm directing it specifically to you. Did you take any documents, recordings, or other material that belonged to the State Security Service in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not take any documents because they're official documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And you say that it would be a crime to remove documentation from the State Security Service; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a crime. Ever since the State Security Service began, not only the State Security Service but also it applies to other services as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's understood. My next question: The republican security service in Bosnia worked on the principle of secrecy; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is one of the principles of operation of the state security service, the principle of secrecy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, you said that you personally did not take any documents because they're official documents. Does that also include that you never copied one and kept it for yourself and took it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not know anything or have access to the documents that the Prosecutor is referring to. I didn't see it. I had no access to it. I didn't make any copies of these documents that were taken from the Zlatiste facility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And just so you know, sir, my question was more broad than that. It wasn't limited to the Zlatiste facility. Is what Judge Orie asked you, would that apply for any documents or recordings? Not just the ones taken from the Zlatiste facility.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This applies to all the documents of the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Going back to the principle of secrecy which we do understand is one of the bedrocks of your service. The application of this principle meant that information about the methods and the techniques used by a department of the service to obtain certain intelligence was compartmentalised so that individuals would be only aware of the information they were specifically authorised to have; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The principle of secrecy and the way documents are kept was different. The documents were not kept in facilities of the RDB but in some other locations that were secret, some other institutions and other places that had a sufficient system of protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for those explanations. I just want to return to your statement and my question from yesterday. I see do you have a copy of the statement with you. Can you confirm that the matters you discuss up to and including paragraph 96 of your statement concern events that supposedly occurred prior to April 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am speaking about those events because they had a crucial effect on what happened after April. The war in Bosnia and Herzegovina did not just break out suddenly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that wasn't the question that was put to you. The question was whether you can confirm that everything, every event found in paragraphs 1 to 96, 96 included, are events which took place before April 1992. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I confirm that except for paragraphs 18 and 19, they all do refer to that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay, sir, thank you for that clarification. I'll look at those during the next break, those paragraphs. We'll come back to your statement in a little bit. But I want to focus on some other matters with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 31531 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, before you is a 10 October 1994 RS MUP request from Nedeljko Kesic for an allocation of an apartment to you. In the second paragraph, Mr. Kesic states that you were: "Among the first people in the former State Security Service of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina ... to organise the Serbian personnel in order to oppose the Croatian-Muslim coalition." Before we discuss a number of other materials today I would just like you to answer openly: Could you tell us how you were one of the first organisers of Serbian personnel to oppose the Croatian-Muslim coalition?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the way it's written but I wouldn't agree with that. You know, when requests of this kind are written, then they are written in affirmative way but I would not attach such importance to myself. However, by the nature of my work I was nearby, and I believe that I was part of this group of people who worked on the establishment of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say you were part of the group of people, who do you consider to be part of that group? If you could tell us the names.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in addition to myself in the State Security Service where I worked, there were a few other colleagues who, in that stage, noticed on time political, military and media preparations for war against the Serbs and --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sorry to cut you off, but I do want to go through things in an efficient manner. If could you just tell us the names of the people that you consider to be part of the group.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to myself in the State Security Service, Mr. Dragan Devedlaka, Goran Radovic operated in this way as well. I would mention the two of them because, as I've said, at that time they were my two closest co-workers who held high positions. And in the centres of state security there were other colleagues, however, that would be a list that would be somewhat longer. Of course, if I need to list all of them, I have the time to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We'll go through and discuss more names so it might be more efficient to just identify them as we go. In the next paragraph it says Mr. Kesic states that you greatly contributed to the creation of the SNB of the RS MUP. Could you explain how you did this?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, precisely this information that I referred to in my statement are part of these activities. As I did my regular work, and as I was in contact with colleagues who were engaged in operative work on the ground, we viewed the overall situation and relations that affected our personal safety and security and the level of imperilment for the people that we represented. We had a professional challenge as well. Not to allow --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you're explaining the circumstances to me, but are there any concrete, direct contributions that you made to the creation of the SNB that you'd like to share with us right now?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I did anything important that would affect my contribution in that direction. I just did not accept to be part of the project that was envisaged by those who headed the State Security Service on the Muslim and Croat sides. I didn't want to be an accomplice in that part of the activities involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right. We will discuss what I'm going to ask you next a little bit more later, but I see in the same paragraph that Mr. Kesic indicates that you were directly engaged in the organisation of the security detail for Radovan Karadzic. Is it correct that you organised security for Mr. Karadzic and other Bosnian Serb officials throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was just one stage of my involvement. In view of my job description in the pre-war State Security Service, because I was chief of the department for providing security for persons and buildings - that is to say, persons coming from the Croat, Serb, and Muslim people - when the war started, a number of operatives who were involved in providing security were within my purview. So I dealt with that work directly especially in relation to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you could just pause there. Finish your sentence: "Especially in relation to ..."

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radovan Karadzic. During his international political activities and the contacts that he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could please listen carefully to my questions and I do have follow-up questions which will allow you to provide further detail. Do I understand from your previous answer that you organised security details for Radovan Karadzic and other Bosnian Serb officials prior to April 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before April 1992, there was a request to expand the list of persons who were provided with security; namely, the presidents of political parties and the heads of religious communities because their security was being endangered increasingly. That was a decision taken by the Assembly of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was on that basis that Karadzic was supposed to have security as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You're speaking in the -- in a certain tense. You say: "Supposed to have security as well." Did you organise, did you personally organise, security details for Radovan Karadzic and other Bosnian Serb officials prior to 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not take part in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the next -- returning to the document, in the next paragraph, there's reference to your service-related changes of residence between Pale, Belgrade, Bijeljina, and Banja Luka. Is it correct that these are the locations where you were stationed throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 31531 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31531 receives number P6881, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6881 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Vlaski, when you were a witness in the Stanisic and Zupljanin case, is it correct that you identified speakers in a number of intercepted communications involving Radovan Karadzic; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 31530 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Coming up will be an 18 September 1991 conversation between Radovan Karadzic and Trifko Komad which you previously authenticated during a proofing session with the Prosecution on the 14th of February, 2010.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution actually go to page 3 of the English and page 4 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Toward the top of the page before you, which is at the bottom of the page in the English, Radovan Karadzic indicates he is meeting with Alija at 2.15 again, and Trifko Komad asks if Rajko is needed there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we scroll down the English please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you see this portion?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the next page of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Radovan Karadzic goes on to state in this conversation: "Yes, I need Rajko and I need some others to get in touch with me. If you can, tell Brana to find them. I need Vlaski and Momo Mandic ..." There's then a discussion of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- you have not read the entirety of this paragraph. And apart from that, what is filled it you just read it as -- if that would be the text, that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- "some others and tell," and you left out the last three words.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: "And tell Momo Mandic to call me." Thank you, Your Honours, for bringing that to my attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There's then a discussion and Devedlaka is also mentioned. Can you please confirm that you are one of the individuals being discussed during this conversation?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm on the basis of this transcript that I am being mentioned too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At that time in September 1991, Dragan Devedlaka was one of your subordinates in the 5th Administration of the DB; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that, he was in my department as an inspector, in the department for providing security for persons and buildings, before this date, before September. It was until May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the question was at that time in September. So you're not asked to tell what Mr. Devedlaka did before or after that but what he did in September. Was he one of your subordinates in the 5th Administration of the DB in September of 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was not my subordinate and he was not in the 5th Administration at this moment, in that period there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us what he did in September 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that period, he was assistant head of the State Security Service of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did Radovan Karadzic know who you were in September 1991?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In September 1991, I was proposed and nominated, appointed deputy head of the State Security Service according to a decision made by Minister Alija Delimustafic. Because on the basis of the agreement reached among the political parties involved, this position was allocated to the Serb people. So that is how Radovan Karadzic found out about the personnel appointments and the equal representation of the peoples of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the basis of the census. Especially for top positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I just get clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, in this position of head of State Security Services, are there two posts, one of assistant and one of deputy; and, if so, what is the difference between the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the rules on internal organisation and job descriptions, there were the following positions: The under-secretary, that is to say, the head of the State Security Service, that was a position that was taken up by a Croat. Then the position of his deputy, the deputy head of the State Security Service. According to the agreement reached among the political parties as one of the important positions, that was allocated to a representative of the Serb people. Whereas within the leadership of the State Security Service, there were two positions, namely, assistant heads of the State Security Service. One was allocated to the Muslims and the other one was allocated to the Serbs, and Mr. Devedlaka held this position at this moment at the time when this transcript came into being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we go back to my question. Were there two different posts, a deputy head of State Security Service and an assistant head of State Security; and, if so, what was the difference? Don't tell me about other posts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The difference was because the deputy head could stand in for the head whereas the assistant heads had specific lines of work that they were in charge of. So in terms of work organisation, one assistant head was in charge of operative, technical matters, whereas the other one was in charge of operative work of other departments. So they were co-ordinators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So at the time that this Mr. Devedlaka was the assistant head of state security, you were the deputy head of state security, in September 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not the deputy but I did receive a decision appointing me to that position. However, I was prevented from assuming that position which is why this political problem was created.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, you were appointed in September 1991. Whatever may have prevented you from taking the position. But at that time you were being appointed as deputy, Devedlaka was the assistant -- was the assistant head of the state security.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wasn't planning to go much into the structure of the DB but just maybe just to clarify one thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that there was an under-secretary of the State Security Service at the republic level, a deputy for that person, and then individual heads of each of the administrations within the security service?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So what is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is that correct? Is that how the State Security Service was structured?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a moment ago I explained that we had a head who was called an under-secretary, that was an anachronism from the previous system. And this head had a deputy head, two assistant heads, and there were the chiefs of the administrations or departments. Yes, so that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. We're on the same page. Going back to September 1991, up until that time, had you ever had any contacts with Radovan Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I did not have any official contact or any private contact in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you in that period. I'm asking you more generally. Did you know him before September 1991?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness says "that period," I understand him to say the period you mentioned, that is, up until September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Right. Which means anytime prior --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if you say: I'm not asking you in that period, then it's ... Did you have any official or private contact with Mr. Karadzic up to September 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not have any contact with Mr. Karadzic. Although, from 1975, I was familiar with his activity because he was a subject of the work of the service that I worked for, and I knew everything about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just want to go back to this conversation. And a little bit further down on the page, about -- Radovan Karadzic then continues to state in this conversation: "We will be deciding on the MUP today." And then he goes on to say after Mr. Komad speaks: "Yes, yes, we are working on the MUP today. Rajko should be told this, and we are working on the MUP today." Were you contacted regarding this work on the MUP?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any contact in view of this situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you aware as to whether Radovan Karadzic wanted to work on the MUP because he wanted to draw up a scheme according to the importance and value of positions to the SDS?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew about that because I felt that problem on my very own skin. As for this part of the schematic, it was part of an inter-party agreement reached and Mr. Rajko Dukic was in charge of that on behalf of the SDS. He was the person who co-ordinated these personnel affairs when the parties that formed the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina had meetings of their personnel commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 31530 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was just going ask, before we do that, whether the witness did go to Radovan Karadzic as stated here that he was required either to call or to come personally. Did you go as a result of this discussion? Did you either call Mr. Karadzic or did you go to see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't go to see him. I did not report there because I was aware of the fact that nothing would come out of that. Radovan Karadzic had no influence over personnel policy in the ministry and in the State Security Service. Even the SDS as such did not have any influence there whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You tell us that you didn't go there. Did the request reach you to go there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard about the request from my colleague Devedlaka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31530 receives number P6882, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 31529 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, coming up before you will be another intercepted conversation from the afternoon of 18 September 1991. This conversation is between Radovan Karadzic and Rajko Dukic. On this first page, we see again that Mr. Karadzic is discussing the 2.15 meeting and then he states: "We have to complete the MUP first and when we are done we will continue working and you can then go. But we have to find out exactly which positions ... firstly, who appoints the staff and, secondly, the arrangement ..." Do you see that portion?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just to -- based on your experience in the service, it was apparent by this time that an ethnic balance would have to be reached at the managerial levels of the MUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ethnic balance was one of the most invaluable principles of the previous communist socialist system of government and the stability of Bosnia-Herzegovina was based on that. So this is just continuity, namely, to honour the ethnic balance and equality of rights of the peoples of Bosnia-Herzegovina everywhere, including this State Security Service. This is a principle upon which Bosnia and Herzegovina was based.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With that being said, is it correct that at this time, by September 1991, that the leaderships of the political parties took over and a sort of deal-making or bartering started where the SDS fought for areas of interest which were really not logical at all?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not logical that in September 1991 this question is being raised at all because the government was established after the 1990 elections and this process was supposed to be completed very quickly after the government was established. However, because of the unequal position of the representatives of the Serb people, this problem escalated in this period of time, especially in the State Security Service. And when Mr. Karadzic said, as far as my very own case was concerned, that this was the last drop, the straw that broke the camel's back, and he would consider leaving all government posts in Bosnia-Herzegovina and that the SDS would consider becoming the government opposition in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We'll come back to that, I think, after the recess.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 31529 into evidence. And, Your Honours, this is a good time for the Prosecution to break if you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31529 receives number P6883, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Witness, we'll take a break of 20 minutes and we'd like to see you back after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, before we take that break, there's some confusion about the deadline you asked for to be extended. Now we extended it, but could you again tell me exactly what the deadline was about. Is it about the request for leave to reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that deadline did not expire today but it expired on the 30th of October. But it is extended anyhow --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay, thanks. I calculated somehow that it should expire today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, at least Chambers' staff thinks that it expired on the 30th of October. Let's not make a drama out of it. There's no opposition from the Prosecution. We'll just --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise if I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's extended as we decided before. We'll take a break, and we'll resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, the Prosecution -- the next document it's going to call up is 65 ter 20261.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is no translation available for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's available now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, to follow your line, thank you to everyone in and around the courtroom, including Ms. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Welcome back, Mr. Vlaski. Before you is another intercepted conversation which you previously authenticated during a meeting with the Prosecution on 3 June 2009. And I see you're nodding your head. It is a conversation between Radovan Karadzic and Miodrag Simovic from 17 September 1991, a day before the last two conversations we looked at. In this conversation, about halfway through the first long answer, Radovan Karadzic states: "Tonight at 8.00, I am going to break up with Izetbegovic. I am withdrawing everything, Serbian Democratic Party into opposition. We are doing [sic] dis to break apart and then we're going to establish our own SUP separately with other men, without ... and we'll make the government separately, we'll make everything separately." My question: Was this what you were talking about before the break, that the SDS would consider becoming the government opposition in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is precisely something that reflects the social reality in Bosnia and Herzegovina at that time, humiliation, over-voting, violating the constitution in the assembly, the procedure. This was something that was happening to such an extent in all the institutions prompting Mr. Karadzic to have this reaction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were not asked what made Mr. Karadzic decide this but you were asked whether this is the development you talked about earlier. And I do understand that you confirm that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I confirmed that earlier. This was just a comment to my previous statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do not comment if no request for further comments are put to you. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In this same discussion, right before the part that I read, there's reference to "Vlaski was removed from his office and it is over." Just so we have clarification, is it correct that that is a reference to you?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you no longer performed your duties at the republican MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina between mid-September 1991 and the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was performing my duties. For a time, I was not deployed in any specific position, but then I was working in the 1st SDB Administration. This was in early 1992. If I can explain, then I can just tell you what happened about all of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We're going to go and discuss early 1992. But just so I could have clarification, between mid-September 1991 and you taking up your position in the 1st SDB Administration in early 1992, is it correct that you did not perform your duties in the Bosnian MUP between that time? You didn't go to work during that time; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to work regularly. However, I didn't have any specific tasks. The decision that I received remained in force, and I received my salary on the basis of that decision. I spent my work hours in the office of Mr. Devedlaka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would tender this intercept into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 20261 receives number P6884, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Vlaski, is it correct that you attended a meeting on 11 February 1992 in Banja Luka with Momcilo Mandic, Mico Stanisic, Stojan Zupljanin, and Zoran Zugic, among others? I see you're nodding your head but if could you please answer.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Goran Zugic. Yes, I was present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This meeting was held at the Bosna hotel; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the minutes of the meeting were taken by Igor Velasevic, who was a lawyer at that time, a young lawyer specifically?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Igor Velasevic was a member of our service. He was employed at the MUP. I think that later he worked as a lawyer. I don't know what happened afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- clear the confusion. "Lawyer" in our language is only somebody who has private practice and has bar exam. And we have different term for somebody who is working in companies or -- or in MUP or somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you want to tell us that he was -- that Igor Velasevic later acted as a lawyer in his own law firm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor said "lawyer," but he was actually working on legal affairs in our service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And later on, he went into private practice as a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P3208 [Realtime transcript read in error "P3028"] for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, coming up will be the minutes of the meeting in Banja Luka on 11 February 1992. I know those minutes have been shown to you before. I was wondering if you could just take a look at them and confirm that these are the minutes of the meeting you attended?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Weber, what is the P number?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's P3208.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. At least it will be corrected now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you confirm that these are the minutes of the meeting you attended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, these are the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 5 of the B/C/S original and page 3 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On this page, we see that you spoke at this meeting, and you started with the comment: "We must work out how to carry out the decisions from this meeting. The only way would be to organise the Serbian MUP and implement all the decisions without questions -- without question." Can you confirm that this is what you said during the meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do I understand correctly from this statement that you were in support of all the conclusions that were reached at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did support the conclusion in the domain of my service. As for those that referred to the work of other participants, I did support them in the political sense, but I did not go into any kind of detailed analysis of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 6 of the B/C/S and page 4 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I want to discuss further with you the conclusions that were reached at this meeting. Under conclusion 1 it is stated: "A Serbian collegium is hereby established in the SRBH MUP, consisting of Serbian personnel at executive positions in all the lines of work within the SRBH MUP." Were you one of these people that received an executive position in the Serbian collegium?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have any functions. We were the personnel of Serbian ethnicity in the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina who were supposed to represent the interest of the Serbian people within a joint MUP. The interests of the Serbian people that were under threat at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: My question --

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this was just the Serb collegium.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. My question was: Did you receive an executive position in the Serb collegium?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No executive positions were given. We were just representatives of the Serb collegium by nature of our ethnicity. We were representatives of the Serbian people and we were working jointly in the collegium as Serbs. We were supposed to form some kind of consultative body made of up of ethnic Serbs but it did not have any kind of executive function.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, is there any chance that there's any confusion about how the words "executive positions" are used here?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's possible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From your question --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From your question, I understand that you read it as the members of the collegium being appointed at executive positions within that collegium. Whereas another way of reading it would be that those in executive positions and being Serbs would become members of the collegium.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think you're right. And I'm happy to rephrase that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I think the witness more or less in his answer has --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I misunderstood, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but there's a chance that you read it in two different ways. I do understand that you now take the position that it should be understood as those who were in executive positions in the SRBH MUP and were Serb, that they would become members of the Serbian collegium.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I actually appreciate your clarifications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under conclusions 2 and 3, the minutes indicate that Momcilo Mandic will manage the Serbian collegium and all staffing policies cannot be implemented without his approval. This was agreed upon at the meeting; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was some sort of desperate need to protect the rights and the interests of the Serbian personnel in the MUP in this way and to then place that under the responsibility of some person in a leading position, and Momcilo Mandic was thought to be such a person at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you're giving me explanations. That was what was agreed upon at this meeting; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see that on the basis of the conclusion, that this is something that was agreed upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the next page in the B/C/S and stay on the same page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just want to go quickly over some of the other items. Under conclusion 13, there's reference to: "Ensuring liaison and providing assistance to the Republic of Serbian Krajina." Did this collegium co-ordinate at all with Milan Martic, the RSK minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that at that point in time there were any indications of any sort of co-ordination, at least as far as this makeup is concerned. I don't know if any of the people involved from the area of Banja Luka had any contacts with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Prior to this meeting, is it correct that you had gone to Belgrade to seek the assistance of Radmilo Bogdanovic, the former head of the Serbian MUP, and Jovica Stanisic, the chief of the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My colleague Devedlaka and I did go to see Mr. Radmilo Bogdanovic but we did not go to see Jovica Stanisic because at that time, Mr. Zoran Janackovic was the one who was heading the RDB.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. So based on the timing that you've given, is it correct that your visits to Radmilo Bogdanovic would have then been before he left office in May of 1991?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And Mr. Stanisic was a member of the Serbian DB, and did you go see him after his official appointment after Mr. Janackovic left at the outset of 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any contacts with Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under conclusion number 16 --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could go -- actually, we need the next page of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under conclusion 16, the minutes state: "Work intensively to train and arm our police personnel." Is it correct that this refers to arming Serb police personnel?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I read the conclusion literally, this is talking about the training and arming of our police personnel, meaning Serb police personnel, because in the previous period, an imbalance was recorded, both in the training and arming of the Serb contingent of personnel in the Ministry of THE Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm -- if could you answer my questions and please listen carefully. I do want to try to conclude you today. I want to change topics and discuss the barricades with you in Sarajevo in March. Can you confirm that you were aware of the setting up of barricades in Sarajevo between the 1st and the 4th of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any information about the setting up of the barricades until the actual moment that they were erected. It was a Sunday that day, and I was skiing at Mount Bjelasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And just so we have a clear record of that, the Sunday that you were skiing, was that the 1st of March?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the 1st of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you learned of the barricades being erected in Sarajevo from Djordje Kapor, one of your colleagues who was providing security for Mr. Karadzic in Belgrade at the time?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, he was the first person to inform me about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct Mr. Kapor called you to inform you of this?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He called me from Belgrade. I was at my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When Mr. Kapor called you, did he convey to you a message from Radovan Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He told me what the problem was in Sarajevo after the killing of the Serbian best man in the wedding party.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you informed that Mr. Karadzic wanted you to go down to the Deputies Club?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the point of the whole conversation, and to assemble.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who was Radovan Karadzic meeting with in Belgrade at the time?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who he was with in Belgrade. I was -- I myself was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. After you received these instructions, is it correct that you then went to the Deputies Club on Djuro Djakovic Street?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct. There were other colleagues there besides me, so based on that, you could call it the Serb collegium.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Just so we have some date context, did you receive this call and go to the Deputies Club on the 1st or 2nd of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was on the 1st of March. It was the same day, after the killing of the person from the Serbian wedding party.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Deputies Club was the official premises used by the deputies of the Serbian Democratic Party; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, all the clubs of national parties had their own premises where they gathered. The club of the Serb deputies was in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. And that's where you went; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went then, but otherwise I did not go to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After you went to the Deputies Club, is it correct that you were then told to go to the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not whether it was said. It's -- it was the conclusion that it was not appropriate for taking measures that followed later. I mean political measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say "it was the conclusion," whose conclusion was this?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, joint conclusion. Most participants assessed that for security reasons this area was not a place where one could stay longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. When you went to the Holiday Inn, did you meet there with Rajko Dukic and Velibor Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. On the premises that Mr. Dukic used as the office of his company, that's where this meeting was held.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And this was in the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mico Stanisic, Dragan Kijac, Dragan Devedlaka, and Momo Mandic were also at the Holiday Inn on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the mentioned persons were at the Holiday Inn. Along with some other individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P6634 for the witness. The Prosecution is looking for page 2 of the B/C/S original and page 3 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, coming up before you is a Socialist Republic of BiH MUP report on the -- on information about the setting up of barricades in Sarajevo in early March 1992. Under item 1, there's information that Momo Mandic was in command at the barricade on the Vrbanja bridge and the deputy commander was Dragisa Kujacic. Is it correct that Mr. Kujacic was also present at the Holiday Inn when you went there?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know him personally, but I was aware of the fact that it had to do with some criminal?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I have -- it sounds like you ended your last answer with a question. It's not clear what you meant by "some criminal"? Did you -- did you want to clarify anything?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot clarify because, I mean, I was not involved in this kind of work in the MUP and also I am not familiar with these roles, commander or deputy commander of barricades. I was not aware of the fact that there was some kind of hierarchy even then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, could we go to page 5 in both versions of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On this page, the report lists five individuals who were engaged. It indicates that Mico Stanisic and Momo Mandic were giving instructions to people in the field. Did Stanisic and Mandic provide instructions or reach any conclusions about the setting up of the barricades at the Holiday Inn while you were present?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, as far as I know, agreements were not being reached on the barricades. Rather, the point of this Crisis Staff was a political message to the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina. How to have this situation overcome. The barricades were a spontaneous reaction on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, did you yourself man barricades?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not at the barricades, and I didn't even visit. But I passed through barricades.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Is it correct that after the barricades were set up by the Serbs, that the Bosnian Muslims then set up their own barricades?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. However, in this report, this information is not contained.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. That's why I was asking it for -- from you, sir. Just so there is no confusion here eventually with this report, it says that -- it appears to refer to you, that Nedjo Vlaski was wounded by fire-arms and he was hospitalised. Is it correct that this was a self-inflicted wound that did not occur at the barricades?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't at the barricades but it had to do with the barricades because I passed through two Muslim barricades and I was armed. And in the weapon, there was a bullet that, due to certain circumstances, happened to hit me in the leg or foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And that was a bullet from your own gun; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time, I'm actually going to move off this document, and I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to play 65 ter 31014 for the witness. And if we could actually, maybe just for time efficiency, go to the 35-second mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a video dated 30 March 1992, and I'm now going to play it. If you could please watch it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could play if from the 35-second mark and pause at 49 seconds. And there's no translation that is necessary for this part of the clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So no audio.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There's no speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No speaking. Okay. That's -- no spoken words. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And we're now paused at the 49-second mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, in this clip we saw that there was a gentleman in a grey overcoat and tie. Is it correct that that person is Mico Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now in this clip, we saw that there were individuals in camouflage uniforms and berets. Is it correct that those are members of the Bosnian Serb MUP?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were active members of the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This is Mr. Zoran Cvijetic, as far as I can see in this footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You've mentioned Mr. Zoran Cvijetic. Is he the person who is currently partially obscured in the lighter colour overcoat in this video or is he the man in the camouflage in the -- to the left of Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person in camouflage uniform, as far as I know, is Mr. Cvijetic, although the face is not very clear here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- one of your previous questions has been answered in an ambiguous way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I defer to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You asked the witness whether these are members of the Bosnian Serb MUP. Now the witness answered by saying: "These were active members of the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Were these all Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose. I don't know who was lined up. I suppose they are Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And under the circumstances on the 30th of March, at such an occasion, you would only find active Serb members of the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina to be lined up like this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that was already the moment when there was a division in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could go to the 3 minute, 40 second mark in the video-clip and pause the video at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going play this for about four seconds, sir, so you can see the images because I see it's a little bit blurry when we have it paused.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm go to ask Ms. Stewart to play to 3 minutes, 44 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, we see that there are individuals in a different type of uniform, a blue uniform. Similar question as before: Were those Serb members of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose. I don't have any reliable proof on the basis of which I can claim that there were no other persons of different ethnicity there, but this is what I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm now going to actually go to Mr. Stanisic's comments on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, a lot of the other video is just the procession of individuals back and forth and an oath being administered by Mr. Cvijetic, so I'm going to skip ahead to Mr. Stanisic's comments at 4 minutes and 3 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, nevertheless, do the parties agree on what kind of an oath was it? To be loyal to the Serb or to the MUP or to the ... is there any ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There's the translation uploaded of it. I can read the oath in. It does refer to the constitution of the Serbian Republic of the Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina is again repeated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's any dispute about that, we'd like to hear. Now, when you earlier said, "I don't know whether there were any people of other ethnicities there," when you were asked about the blue uniforms, but the uniforms themselves, they were of -- of the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The SUP -- the Serb MUP did not have uniforms then. These were uniforms that were used by the active and reserve policemen. I saw the uniforms there. Possibly Mr. Cvijetic had some kind of insignia but it is rather blurred and I didn't see it very clearly. Otherwise this is the first time I'm watching this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But it is -- when you say "were used by active and reserve policemen," you mean active and reserve policemen of Serbian ethnicity, of the Serbian --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the joint police used the same uniforms because up until this moment, the 30th of March, all of these persons, who I assume were there for this lineup, were part of the regular MUP, either active duty or reserve.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, you -- earlier when I put to you a question focused very much on this matter, what you would expect people to be lined up, you said: It was after the -- there was a division already in the Ministry of Interior. So you then explained that what we see is for that reason most likely Serbian, whereas now asked about these uniforms on the same day, you see -- you say it could be the joint police forces. That is -- there's some friction between the two. Could you explain why you are having more reservations as far as the uniforms you saw being worn by Serb police officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, on the uniforms, it doesn't say who is a Serb, who is a Bosniak, who is a Croat. Everybody wore the same uniforms when they worked in the previous joint MUP, in the previous joint institutions. There was a similar situation as far as uniforms are concerned. Only insignia were changed on caps, on epaulettes and so on. We did not have the resources, I mean, to change uniforms for the entire force, for the sake of this kind of situation, when there would be a lineup, a review or oath-taking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if I understand you well, you're saying the setting is such that there should be no more doubt as whether those wearing uniforms there were Serbs than compared to what you said earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I assumed that they were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to play the remainder of the clip. I believe transcripts have been disseminated to the booths, and there is audio for this portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we need to play it twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours -- Your Honours, this time the Prosecution is going to play it the second time

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do as you suggest.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "As of today, the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina has its own police force. The legality of our existence is provided by the constitution of the Assembly of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Law on Internal Affairs recently adopted by the Assembly at its session. Moreover, the legality of our existence is based on the result of negotiations of the three ethnic communities under the auspices of the European community. As of today, we will act as the police of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina which will carry out its tasks and assignments professionally and not politically, as the MUP of the old Bosnia and Herzegovina has done so far, in order to protect property, life, body, and overall security of all citizens in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina equally. "Members of the police, we are not involved in politics. We must carry out our tasks professionally. Therefore, long speeches do not belong to us, but as of today, good luck, get to work, in the interest of all who live in the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Thank you."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I think you've alluded to this already, but can you confirm that as of the 30th of March, 1992, that the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina had its own police force?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was just a public manifestation of that act. Its existence was defined in the constitution and the Law on Internal Affairs as was stated at this gathering. The law and the constitution of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And that constitution and law were passed on the 28th of February, 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the sequence of events that preceded this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Aside from Mr. Cvijetic who you've previously mentioned, did you recognise any of the other individuals who were present on the stage with Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognised Mr. Cicko Bjelica whom I do not know personally, but I recognised him in this footage because he was a Member of Parliament and some SDS functionary.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders 65 ter 31014 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe Ms. Stewart does have CDs available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, now having received the CDs, what number would be assigned?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31014 receives number P6885, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 31533 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, coming up is an 30 April 1992 SRBiH MUP list of employees of the Trnovo police station. You are the first person on this list which indicates that you were the chief of the Trnovo police station. Is it correct that you held this position in April and early May 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never the chief. I don't know who compiled this list. However, at that moment, due to that circumstance, the fact that I was wounded, I was in the area because this is where I was born.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, did you have any activities related to the Trnovo police in April and May 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not carry out any activities at the station, but I was involved in the peace council that was established in the municipality of Trnovo because I was a colleague of the head of that station at the time of the joint service, I mean, the joint MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Godinjak. I worked with Edo Godinjak for many years. So I was involved in that sense, in the area of this municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. And, sir, I want to be fair to you and we had two different lists that related to this police station so I do want to show you the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 3 of the B/C/S and page 4 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is an SRBiH MUP CSB Trnovo list of active police workers who carried out duties during the month of April 1992. You are the first person again on the list. And the document indicates that you were paid out in the SNB. Is it correct that you were a member of the SNB as of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. However, due to the fact that I was wounded for a while, I was in that area for 15, 20 days, and these colleagues from the public security station of Trnovo put me there for the sake of continuity so that I could get this compensation that our ministry was paying anyway, of the Serb ministry. However, as is stated here, I was paid through the SNB where I was assistant head.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are those your initials or signature on that first line to the far right, under the fifth column? Are you able to see them?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I see this document. I never signed anything on this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- could I -- you say you never signed. Does this appear to be your signature or is your signature entirely different from this one? It could be a forgery produced by someone else, but does it resemble in any way your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My signature is not here. It is noted that I was paid out in the SNB, meaning that the salary was paid due to my affiliation with the service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You have still not answered my question. That is, whether what appears here in column 5, whether that resembles or does not resemble your signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't see my signature anywhere here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And nothing that looks like your signature either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, nothing like that. I did not sign anything on a document of this kind, ever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You apparently are very insistent on answering your own question rather than mine. But I take it that what appears on this document is not similar to what is your signature. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, sir, you've acknowledged that you were paid out from the SNB at this time. Is it correct that someone could have just simply signed for you on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can see, there is no signature here. It's just a colon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to intervene. It says, I will spell, i-s-p-l.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. One second. Mr. Lukic, you intervened when the previous translation was still continuing. Apparently you wanted to bring something to our attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. It says, I will spell, i-s-p-l, which is shortened for "isplacen," paid, and it's not the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In English translation it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
